direct_claims: This chart reports results from a task-based usability test with 11 interpretive tasks.
The figure comes from a CHI 2021 paper.
Each percentage represents the share of participants who were able to partially or fully succeed in completing that task.
The lowest-success task is determining the direction the arrow is pointing, at 0.0%.

The reported percentages include both partial and full success, so they reflect whether participants could make meaningful progress on a task, not necessarily whether every response was perfectly correct.
Because this figure comes from a usability study, the results matter for evaluating whether people can accurately interpret slide content under the tested conditions.
The two tasks involving relative position between objects both have the same success rate of 36.4%.
The chart does not provide sample size, participant characteristics, or the interface conditions of the test, which limits how confidently these results can be generalized.
